findings.text: The set thread id address system entry records a user pointer for clearing the child thread identifier at exit and reports the callers numeric thread identifier in its own namespace.
A pid file descriptor preparation interface accepts a process identifier with creation flags and on success yields an installed descriptor plus a file object, otherwise a negative failure indicator.
A seccomp filter acquisition interface shares the callers active filter with the target task by elevating reference and user accounting, doing nothing when no filter is present.

A duplicated memory descriptor when successfully created is an independent copy of the parent descriptor with duplicated mappings and recorded peak usage. Failure yields absence without partial installation.

New tasks begin with cleared fault and switch accounting and without memory linkage. Kernel threads without parent memory stay memoryless. Virtual memory sharing implies joint use with extra accounting, otherwise the child owns a duplicate that becomes both its memory and active memory.
Execution state follows virtual memory sharing. Shared mode implies joint reference with elevated count, otherwise the child receives a fresh independent copy.

Filesystem context is either jointly used with elevated user count or independently copied. Joint use is refused during exec transitions. Helper contexts face added namespace and sharing limits and use the initial filesystem.
File tables are either jointly used with elevated count or duplicated. Missing parent tables or an explicit no files request imply absence in the child.

Signal handler state is either jointly used with elevated count or freshly allocated as a copy of parent actions. An explicit clearing request forces copied non ignored entries to default disposition.
After handler reset every signal slot shows default disposition when forced or when not previously ignored, with cleared options and an empty mask.

Thread creation shares the signal descriptor. Other creation yields a fresh descriptor representing a sole thread with initialized linkage, waiting, pending, timing, limit, auditing, grouping, out of memory and synchronization members.
Group processor timers start from the current processor time limit observed at fork.
Seccomp state is inherited by sharing the parent filter. No new privilege status and syscall work marking follow the parent mode so that filtering remains active in the child.
Filter sharing is a no action when absent. Otherwise both the filter reference count and the user count are elevated.
Process identifier linkage starts empty for every identifier type. Thread private identifiers reside in the task itself while other types reside in the shared signal descriptor.
A new task begins with cleared read copy update tracking and empty holdout and exit linkage. Priority inheritance locking starts initialized with no waiters and no top task and no blocking relation.

Descriptor creation requires existing task linkage for the requested identifier kind unless stale creation is allowed. Leader descriptors require leader linkage. Allocation or file creation failure prevents installation.

Task memory reclamation is either deferred through read copy update when memory grouping is enabled or performed immediately otherwise. Deferred reclamation retrieves the task from the callback header.

Out of memory score adjustment propagation applies only to memory owning children with virtual memory sharing but without thread or fork wait semantics. Qualifying children are marked multiprocess and refresh their scores under mutual exclusion.
Runtime verification fork handling has alternate build configurations with clearing behavior in one and no action in the other.
Default futex hash allocation is required exactly for siblings that will share the parent memory.

Creation is refused when namespace unsharing is combined with filesystem sharing, when user namespace unsharing is combined with filesystem sharing, when threading lacks shared handlers, when shared handlers lack shared memory, when parent inheritance meets unkillable init state, and when threading meets user or process identifier namespace changes or differing pid namespaces.

Additional refusals cover pid file descriptors combined with detached mode, automatic reaping combined with threading or parent inheritance or an exit signal, parent inheritance under automatic reaping, no new privileges combined with threading, and descriptor auto kill without both descriptor and reaping support or with threading or without privilege when new privileges remain possible.

Creation proceeds through validation, signal quiescence with deferred multiprocess delivery, task duplication, ordered subsystem inheritance, identifier allocation, descriptor preparation, grouping permission and placement, and shared memory support allocation before visibility. Any failure aborts with unwinding and without a visible task.
Signals pending before duplication abort creation with a restart indication after recalculating pending state, preventing a child that would miss pre fork delivery ordering.
Mapping or module acquisition failure during memory duplication leaves no installed descriptor, suppresses module release accounting, clears ownership and balances tracing sessions.
Filesystem sharing attempted while the parent is in an exec transition fails with a retry indication rather than sharing an unstable root and working directory.

The shared signal descriptor aggregates thread counts and liveness, thread list linkage, child exit waiting, current target, shared pending set, multiprocess queue, statistics sequencing, processor time history, timer lists and real timer, resource limits, processor timers, out of memory tunables, credential guarding and execution update synchronization plus thread group cgroup control.

Fork initialized task state spans accounting counters, memory and execution pointers, filesystem and file and handler and signal references, identifier linkage and group identity, child identifier pointers, inheritance and worker flags, locking and pending and timing members, input output and audit and grouping context, memory policy, tracing, fault control and reclamation linkage.
Copying parent handler actions requires holding the parent handler spin lock with interrupts disabled across the copy.
Checking exec status and elevating the filesystem user count requires holding the filesystem sequence lock in exclusive mode across both operations.
Copying resource limits from the group leader requires holding the leader task lock across the copy.
Linking the deferred multiprocess node for non thread creation and recalculating pending signals requires holding the parent handler spin lock with interrupts disabled.

Checking task linkage for process and thread group leader identifiers requires holding the identifier wait queue spin lock with interrupts disabled via scoped guarding unless stale creation bypasses the checks.
Marking multiprocess memory and refreshing out of memory scores requires holding the global adjustment mutex across both updates.
Inheriting seccomp filtering requires the caller to already hold the parent handler spin lock, ensuring stable filter and privilege state during the copy.

ABI clone control names observed are CLONE_VM and CLONE_FS and CLONE_FILES and CLONE_SIGHAND and CLONE_THREAD and CLONE_PARENT and CLONE_NEWNS and CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_NEWPID and CLONE_PIDFD and CLONE_DETACHED and CLONE_AUTOREAP and CLONE_NNP and CLONE_PIDFD_AUTOKILL and CLONE_VFORK and CLONE_CHILD_SETTID and CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID and CLONE_CLEAR_SIGHAND.
ABI signal names observed are SIG_IGN and SIG_DFL and SIGKILL and SIGSTOP with a total count name _NSIG governing handler table iteration.
ABI pid file descriptor names observed are PIDFD_STALE and PIDFD_THREAD and PIDFD_AUTOKILL with descriptor modes O_CLOEXEC and O_RDWR governing creation.
ABI failure indicators observed are ENOMEM and EINVAL and EAGAIN and ESRCH and ENOENT and EPERM and ERESTARTNOINTR indicating allocation and validation and limit and liveness and privilege outcomes.
